subject: history_social
passage: Around 300 BCE, the Greek envoy Megasthenes spent time at Pataliputra, the capital of the Maurya ruler Chandragupta, and afterward wrote an account of India called the Indica. The work itself has not survived. What historians possess instead are passages quoted or paraphrased by later Greek and Roman writers such as Strabo and Arrian, who selected what interested them and sometimes ridiculed what they doubted. Modern knowledge of the Indica is therefore thoroughly ______: every sentence attributed to Megasthenes reaches us through the judgment of someone else.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The text explains that the Indica is lost and that historians have only passages "quoted or paraphrased by later" writers who chose what to include. The colon clause restates the idea: every sentence reaches us "through the judgment of someone else." The blank must mean "passed through an intermediary," which is "mediated."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never says the quoted passages are invented; it says only that they were chosen and filtered by later writers. "Fabricated" claims far more than the text supports.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Later writers "selected what interested them," so what survives is partial, not complete.
explanation.C: Correct. Knowledge that comes to us through other writers' selections and paraphrases is "mediated," exactly as the colon clause explains.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The point of the text is that nothing reaches us directly from Megasthenes; it all comes secondhand.
